chat_obo_intro: The On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flow exchange allows the AI agent to act securely in the system by adopting the user's authority, validated via the act claim.
chat_arch_note_title: Architectural Note: Separation of Duties (Human vs. Agent)
chat_arch_note_p1: This panel compares three tokens, each scoped to a different actor and purpose. The User token (Authorization Code) carries the human's interactive scopes in this app; the Agent token (Client Credentials) is the assistant's own machine identity; and the OBO token (RFC 8693 exchange) is minted for a single delegated action, carrying only the *_agent scope that action needs — bound to both the user (sub) and the agent (act).
chat_arch_note_p2: So why dedicated *_agent scopes instead of reusing create_meeting? Because an application should request only the scopes each actor actually needs for the task at hand. Giving the agent its own action scopes keeps agent-initiated work separate and attributable — every delegated operation traces back to both the user and the executing agent — and ensures the agent only ever holds the narrow scope for the action just authorized, never the user's full interactive set. It's separation of responsibilities, not one global privilege level.
chat_obo_desc: This OBO JWT is issued by WSO2 IS, containing the authorized agent's actor details in the act claim.
chat_agent_desc: This is the AI Agent's system-level client credential token, which authorizes it to request the user's OBO flow.
